uncited: Interpolation schemes for volume rendering reconstruct a continuous scalar field from discrete voxel data to evaluate density or opacity at arbitrary query positions along viewing rays.
This family solves the problem of discretization artifacts (aliasing, blockiness) inherent in nearest-neighbor sampling while balancing computational cost against spatial smoothness.

It sets itself apart from sibling techniques like [Multi-Sample Anti-Aliasing via Ray Distribution](1219-multi-sample-anti-aliasing-via-ray-distribution.md) by focusing on the spatial reconstruction kernel itself rather than the statistical distribution of sample points, and from [Depth to Distance Conversion](2428-depth-to-distance-conversion.md) by operating in voxel space rather than depth space.
Adaptive Interpolation for Isosurface Detection interpolates input volume along rays at a predetermined sampling rate.
The concept of interpolation in volume rendering originated with the need to handle the discrete nature of voxel data in ray-casting algorithms.
